anchor: ask, collect, show, tell: every investigation starts with a fair question and ends with what the data shows

lessons.focus: Ask: statistical questions, fair survey questions with a choice for everyone, categorical and numerical data. Critical feature: a fair question does not push and fits everyone. Review: coordinates and angles (Weeks 1 and 2).

Collect: run a class survey, record with tallies, build a frequency table and check the total. Critical feature: every response counted once; the total equals the number asked. Review: coordinates and angles (Weeks 1 and 2).

Show: choose and draw column graphs, dot plots and line graphs with a title, labels and an even scale. Critical feature: match the display to the data. Review: Cartesian plane, angles, fractions, decimals and percentages.

Tell: interpret displays, spot a misleading graph and write conclusions supported by the data. Critical feature: read the scale before you compare. Review: coordinates, angles, fractions, decimals and percentages.
